hypothesis: A trend-following signal can be premature if a material observed 6s pullback is still opposing an established prior trend, even though the latest 2s reaction agrees with the signal.

fixedRule.priorTrend: Received source observations from t-90s through t-6s, one actual quote per source second, at least 40 observations and 60s coverage, no gap over 3s.
fixedRule.strongTrend: Log-price/time linear R-squared >=0.70, reusing the released range detector's strong-trend boundary.
fixedRule.pullback: Signed last-6s log move against the prior trend larger than twice the median positive absolute prior one-step log move, using the released swing detector's two-change scale.
fixedRule.action: At the final output only, withhold a ready signal only when its side follows that strong prior trend while the pullback still opposes it. Preserve all countertrend, range, unknown and other-duration decisions. Admit nothing new; add no timer; active signals remain immutable.
fixedRule.developmentGoNoGo: Screen original entries before full replay: must remove more losses than wins in EACH of known Forex and both known crypto lots; if not, reject at development and do not consume the new validation set. This screen alone never validates shifted runtime admissions.

validationRegisteredBeforeOutcomes.source: Official Binance 1s closing observations, not broker Digital/OTC settlements. Only evaluate if development screen passes unchanged.

caveats: No guarantee of improvement or 30s foresight.
All development data are already known.
Price-path diagnostic uses future prices only after the original decision and cannot be used as a real-time signal.
